query: Earlier refractory high-entropy alloys illustrate persistent trade-offs: MoNbTaW and MoNbTaVW retained good yield strength from 600 to 1600 °C, with MoNbTaVW reaching 842 MPa at 1000 °C, but both had poor room-temperature fracture toughness and high density; HfNbTaTiZr showed room-temperature ductility above 50% and a yield strength of 929 MPa but only 295 MPa at 1000 °C; and as-cast HfMoTaTiZr achieved about 1600 MPa at room temperature and 855 MPa at elevated temperature but retained a density of 10.21 g cm−3. Given the constraint that density must be reduced without sacrificing the strong room- and high-temperature mechanical performance of as-cast HfMoTaTiZr, what single intervention should be tested? Provide a mechanistic hypothesis, predicted outcomes relative to the as-cast baseline, explicit temperature and loading boundary conditions, supporting evidence from the preceding RHEA results, and a controlled experiment with quantitative rejection criteria that could falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Substituting a portion of Mo with Ti in as-cast HfMoTaTiZr will reduce the density while maintaining strong room- and high-temperature mechanical performance due to the alloying effects of the lighter Ti on the overall density and the preservation of the solid-solution strengthening mechanism.
generation.intervention: substitution of 20% of Mo with Ti
generation.conditions: room temperature to 1600 °C, yield strength loading
generation.mechanism: alloying effects on density and mechanical properties
generation.predicted_outcome: a reduction in density by 5% to 9.65 g cm−3 and maintenance of yield strength above 1500 MPa at room temperature and above 800 MPa at 1000 °C
generation.baseline: as-cast HfMoTaTiZr with a density of 10.21 g cm−3, room-temperature yield strength of 1600 MPa, and 1000 °C yield strength of 855 MPa
generation.boundary: temperature range from room temperature to 1600 °C, loading conditions up to yield strength
generation.uncertainty: The actual reduction in density and the maintenance of mechanical properties may vary based on the exact substitution ratio and the resulting microstructure.

falsification_experiment.design: controlled substitution experiment with varying percentages of Mo replaced by Ti in as-cast HfMoTaTiZr, followed by density and mechanical property measurements
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: if the density is not reduced by at least 3% or if the room-temperature yield strength falls below 1400 MPa or the 1000 °C yield strength falls below 750 MPa, the hypothesis is falsified
